summary: In Greek mythology, Coronus (Ancient Greek Κόρωνος) of Gyrton is the Lapith king, son of Caeneus (or in some accounts Actor), counted among the Argonauts and father of Leonteus. Homer sets him in the Catalogue of Ships stemma; Apollodorus and Hyginus put him on Jason's crew; he later wars on Aegimius and falls to Heracles.

sections.heading: Lapith Argonaut
paragraphs: Homer (Iliad 2.735–746) makes Leonteus son of Coronus son of Caeneus among the Lapith captains from Argissa and Gyrtone. Hyginus (Fabulae 14) and Apollodorus (1.9.16) number Coronus son of Caeneus from Gyrton among the Argonauts. Apollodorus (2.7.7) and Diodorus have him slain by Heracles while leading war against Aegimius.

Bibliotheca 1.9.16 also lists a Caeneus son of Coronus from Gortyn — the atlas keeps that thinner Argonaut as caeneus-gortyn, distinct from the famous Lapith caeneus-lapith who is this Coronus' father.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: Wikipedia's Coronus page lists a Sicyonian son of Apollo, a Corinthian founder of Coroneia, and minor fathers. The atlas id coronus-gyrton is the Lapith of Gyrton alone.
